title: Magyar Government Day Two — EU Fund Reform Deadline Set, ICC Rejoining Submitted, State Media Audit Launched
detail: On May 11, the second full day of the Magyar government, the new administration confirmed a series of first-week reform commitments. The government formally set end-of-May 2026 as the internal deadline for submitting the rule-of-law reform package to the European Commission, the threshold required to trigger the political deal to unlock €17B in frozen EU funds ahead of the August 31 RRF cutoff. Hungary's official EPPO membership application (submitted alongside inauguration day decrees on May 9) was registered at the European Public Prosecutor's Office. The government also ordered an independent audit of the public broadcaster MTVA and the KESMA media foundation, both dominated by pro-Orbán editorial leadership, as a preliminary step toward editorial independence. International media provided extensive follow-on coverage of the May 9 swearing-in, with multiple foreign correspondents in Budapest describing the transition as the most significant democratic correction in Central Europe since Poland's 2023 election. Finance Minister András Kármán held initial meetings with European Commission counterparts to map the accelerated EU funds release roadmap.

media.caption: The Magyar government's first days focus on EU fund reform milestones, EPPO membership, and state media audit
